memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He must have all the inside walls of the house scraped and the material that is scraped off dumped into an unclean place outside the town. Then they are to take other stones and put them in the place of the first ones, and take new clay and plaster the house." - Lev 14:41-42 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Removal is not the end of the work. New stones go in. New plaster goes on. The hole is filled.

That is a crucial pattern, and we miss it often. It is not enough to take something out of our lives; something must take its place. Jesus told a sobering story about a house swept clean and left empty — and what had been driven out came back with reinforcements (Matt 12:43-45). An empty space does not stay empty.

Paul writes this way constantly. Put off falsehood and speak truthfully (Eph 4:25). Anyone who has been stealing must steal no longer, but must work... that they may have something to share (Eph 4:28). Never just stop. Always replace.

So if you are giving something up, ask what is going in its place. Cut down the scrolling — and put in what? Leave the friendships that pulled you away — and build which ones instead? Stop the habit — and fill those hours with what?

The Christian life is not mainly about subtraction. It is about being transformed by the renewing of your mind (Rom 12:2). New stones. New plaster. A house rebuilt, not merely emptied.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have you removed from your life without replacing it?
2. What good thing could fill the space you have cleared?
3. Where do you need renewal rather than just restraint?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, do not let me settle for an empty house. Where You have removed something, fill the space with what is good, and renew my mind by Your Spirit. Amen.
